title: Psalm 36: In Thy Light Shall We See Light

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Welcome to Psalm Nights. [pause 25]

Let the lights go out, one by one. Let your eyes close when they are ready. [pause 25]

Tonight we read part of Psalm 36. Five verses about how big God's kindness is. Bigger than the sky. Deeper than the sea. [pause 25]

We will read them slowly, and then once more. [pause 25]

verses.text: Thy mercy, O LORD, is in the heavens; and thy faithfulness reacheth unto the clouds.
Thy righteousness is like the great mountains; thy judgments are a great deep: O LORD, thou preservest man and beast.
How excellent is thy lovingkindness, O God! therefore the children of men put their trust under the shadow of thy wings.
They shall be abundantly satisfied with the fatness of thy house; and thou shalt make them drink of the river of thy pleasures.
For with thee is the fountain of life: in thy light shall we see light.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
His mercy reaches to the heavens. Look up on a clear night and the sky goes on and on. His mercy reaches that far. [pause 36]

His judgments are a great deep. There are things about God we cannot reach the bottom of. That is all right. [pause 36]

People find shelter under the shadow of his wings. Then a river of pleasures, and a fountain of life. [pause 36]

And in his light, we see light. [pause 36]

A few companion verses. [pause 36]

verses.text: Keep me as the apple of the eye, hide me under the shadow of thy wings,
I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.
Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
The apple of the eye. Hidden under his wings. An old prayer for the night. [pause 36]

And Jesus called himself the light of the world, and said the one who follows him will not walk in darkness. [pause 36]

Here is the reading from Psalm 36 again. Think of the sky above the roof. [pause 36]

verses.text: Thy mercy, O LORD, is in the heavens; and thy faithfulness reacheth unto the clouds.
Thy righteousness is like the great mountains; thy judgments are a great deep: O LORD, thou preservest man and beast.
How excellent is thy lovingkindness, O God! therefore the children of men put their trust under the shadow of thy wings.
They shall be abundantly satisfied with the fatness of thy house; and thou shalt make them drink of the river of thy pleasures.
For with thee is the fountain of life: in thy light shall we see light.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
The reading is done. [pause 8]

Let the last verse settle like dust after a long day on the road. [pause 12]

You have prayed tonight, even if you said nothing. Listening is a kind of prayer. [pause 12]

Let go of the clock. Let go of tomorrow's list. [pause 15]

Under the same sky, many others are lying down tonight, and the same God is with each one. [pause 20]

Peace to you. [pause 45]

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Stored KJV pasted by code; short echoes only; Jesus's and God's words given indirectly outside scripture (light of the world, fear not). Each night keeps its psalm's point (God gives his beloved sleep, waiting for morning, confession and the hiding place, mercy to the heavens, fret not, out of the pit, tears in his bottle, wings in the cave, the Lord good to all, into thine hand). Psalm 127's 'giveth sleep' framed as God's gift, not a promise to the listener; no outcome promises in the new rest.

cultural.note: Plain English; work and worry, fear and shame named with kindness; Ruth named as a foreign widow with dignity; Psalm 31 'commit my spirit' explained with a child's picture, not morbid; pacing by silence (13.5-13.7 min voiced at the measured 117 wpm).
